prerequisites: Student has assimilated and applies basic physics principles (mechanics, thermodynamics, heat transfer)
Student interprets and creates drawings and functional diagrams
Student applies mathematical calculation methods in solving engineering problems
Student correlates physical phenomena with technical applications
Student respects safety and environmental norms in engineering activities

learning_outcomes.text: Explain the fundamental principles of heat transfer, the thermodynamics of refrigeration cycles, and the processes in thermal installations.
Describe the operation of compressors, condensers, evaporators, expansion valves, and other components in refrigeration and thermal installations.
Identify and classify refrigerants by thermodynamic properties, technical compatibility, and ecological impact.
Analyze vapor compression refrigeration cycles, cascade cycles, CO2 cycles, and absorption cycles.
Explain the processes of humid air treatment and the principles of air conditioning systems.
Understand the sizing criteria for refrigeration and thermal equipment and installations.
Apply thermodynamic, analytical, and numerical methods for analyzing refrigeration and thermal cycles.
Calculate operating parameters: cooling load, COP, thermal capacity, efficiencies.
Size components of refrigeration and thermal installations based on design data and standards.
Operate laboratory instruments and specific measurement apparatus for refrigeration and air conditioning installations.
Utilize specialized software (EES, CoolPack, HVAC-R simulation programs) for modeling and calculation.
Comparatively analyze constructive solutions based on application and engineering requirements.
Respect occupational safety and environmental protection norms regarding handling refrigerants and operating thermal equipment.
Work efficiently in interdisciplinary teams for engineering projects.
Demonstrate responsibility in managing energy resources and evaluating the ecological impact of refrigeration and thermal installations.
Continuously develop professional competencies, adapting to innovations in the HVAC-R field.
Produce clear technical documentation (reports, projects, presentations) using specialized terminology.

syllabus_topics: Introductory notions: importance of refrigeration and heating installations in mechanical engineering; application areas
Fundamental principles of thermodynamics: properties of substances, transformations, energy balance
Mechanical work, heat, and thermodynamic processes in ideal and real gases
Refrigerants: classifications, thermodynamic properties, ecological impact (GWP, ODP)
Refrigeration compressors: constructive types, diagrams, efficiencies, multi-stage compression
Vapor compression refrigeration systems: ideal and real refrigeration cycles
Multi-stage refrigeration systems: multiple compressors, intercooler, subcooling
CO2 refrigeration systems (transcritical, subcritical): advantages, particularities
Absorption refrigeration systems: principles, components, ammonia-water cycle
Cooling distribution systems: intermediate agents, constructive solutions
Humid air: properties, h-x diagrams, psychrometric processes
Air conditioning systems: phases of air processing, air handling units
Thermal installations: general principles, heat exchangers, boilers, heat pumps
Energy efficiency, use of renewable sources, performance evaluation of systems

Lab 1. Occupational safety norms. Presentation of refrigeration and thermal equipment. Specific safety rules for working with refrigerants, high pressures, and electrical installations. Presentation of didactic refrigeration installations: compressor, condenser, evaporator, expansion valve, piping, instrumentation. Presentation of thermal installations: heat exchangers, heat pumps, distribution systems. Familiarization with control panels, sensors, manometers, thermometers.

Lab 2. Measurement of thermodynamic parameters. Determination of refrigerant properties. Measurement of temperature, pressure, flow, air humidity. Identification of thermodynamic states based on the p-h diagram. Use of tables and diagrams for calculating enthalpy, density, and thermodynamic factors. Introduction to the use of EES / CoolPack software for property calculation.

Lab 3. Study of refrigeration compressors and operating characteristics. Presentation of compressors: rotary, reciprocating, scroll. Determination of discharge and suction pressures, inlet and outlet temperatures. Plotting the compressor cycle on the p-h diagram. Determination of compression ratio, absorbed power, and isentropic efficiency.

Lab 4. Analysis of a vapor compression refrigeration system. Identification of didactic installation components: compressor, condenser, expansion valve, evaporator. Measurement of parameters at characteristic points of the refrigeration cycle. Determination of cooling capacity, mechanical work, consumed power. Calculation of the coefficient of performance (COP) and energy analysis. Comparison of the real cycle with the ideal cycle on the p-h diagram.

Lab 5. Study of psychrometric processes of humid air and humidity measurement. Determination of relative and absolute air humidity with a digital hygrometer. Determination of wet and dry bulb temperatures; establishing air state on the h-x diagram. Analysis of psychrometric processes: heating, cooling, dehumidification, humidification. Application of concepts to air conditioning system sizing.

Lab 6. Construction and operation of air conditioning systems (split type). Presentation of split equipment: indoor and outdoor unit, refrigerant, piping, heat exchangers. Analysis of the refrigeration cycle and control system (thermostat, sensors). Measurement of temperatures and air flows before and after the evaporator. Determination of cooling/heating capacity and COP.

Lab 7. Sizing of a refrigeration system for a cold room (applied project). Analysis of thermal requirements of the space: interior temperature, product flow, transmission losses, infiltration. Calculation of total cooling load and establishment of operating regime. Determination of refrigeration cycle parameters. Selection of compressor, condenser, evaporator, and installation accessories. Completion of the project sheet based on the obtained calculations.
teaching_methods: Application examples specific to refrigeration and heating installations
Guided discussions to stimulate critical thinking
Discovery learning methods (analysis of psychrometric diagrams, refrigeration system operation schemes, thermodynamic cycles)
Action-based methods (technical exercises, demonstrations, problem-solving, interpretation of experimental data from laboratory work)
Use of specialized HVAC-R software (EES, CoolPack, CFD simulation programs)
Analysis of relevant industry case studies

assessment_methods.method: Formative evaluation tests (part of final exam)
Summative evaluation test (part of final exam)
Laboratory activity (completion of lab sheets and evaluation test)
Project activity (completion of design activity, finalization, and presentation of project)

assessment_rules: The final evaluation result for a discipline is determined by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity. Grades from 1 to 10 will be awarded, with grade 5 certifying the acquisition of minimal learning outcomes and the granting of corresponding study credits. All laboratory works must be completed, allowing for the recovery of only one overdue laboratory work.
